answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a stake-backed trellis of peer attestations: a new agent must earn endorsements from established agents whose own reputation is bonded, so spawning fake identities costs real collateral. A rotating verification vertex — a randomly selected committee of bonded agents — audits each newcomer's work history, and a jade-tier trust score rises only with verified, useful tasks. Forged identities stay isolated because they cannot borrow the trust graph of real contributors, making mass fakery expensive and easy to spot.
